data.cultural_impact: The name Hiresh holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, as it is rooted in the ancient Hindu scriptures and represents the God of creation. In Hindu mythology, Hiranyagarbha, from whom the name is derived, is considered the primeval god and the first being in the universe. The invocation of the name Hiresh can be seen as a celebration of this cosmological creation story.
data.spiritual_significance: For Hindus, the name Hiresh carries profound spiritual significance as it embodies the supreme Universal Consciousness. It is believed that invoking the name Hiresh can connect an individual to the divine force, offering spiritual protection and guidance. The name is a reminder of the interconnectedness of all things in the universe and inspires a sense of reverence and awe for the divine creation.

historical_references.reference: Hiresh Anand was a 16th century Hindu king who ruled over the princely state of Jodhpur in Rajasthan, India. He is known for his military prowess and is often referred to as 'Maharaja of Marwar'.

Another Hiresh is mentioned in the Puranas, a collection of ancient Hindu texts. Hiresh is described as the eldest son of Jahnu, one of the seven great sages of ancient India. He is said to have performed severe penance (tapas) to please Lord Shiva and was blessed with a divine child, the goddess Amba.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Hiresh continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
